sources.citation: Bleek, Dorothea F. 1937. Grammatical notes and texts in the ǀauni language. Bantu Studies 11(1): 253-258. DOI 10.1080/02561751.1937.9676054 (same text as pp. 195ff. of Rheinallt Jones & Doke (eds), Bushmen of the Southern Kalahari, Wits UP 1937).
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: Harvard print copy (Scan & Deliver or loan); the journal or volume is held, not the item itself: TOZ SPEC.COLL. AFR.SOUTH J 718 b
sources.note: Silent on stress, tone and accent. The entire phonological statement is one paragraph on p. 253: "All five clicks are found in ǀauo, the dental and lateral ones being the most frequent, which is not the case in the ǀxam Bushman. The other sounds used are much the same; t and k often turn into tj and kj. For the indefinite sound between r and l I have used Professor Doke's symbol ɽ." The rest (pp. 253-255) is possessives, plurals, numerals, pronouns and verbal particles; pp. 256-258 are four texts. No word 'stress', 'tone', 'accent' or 'pitch' occurs in pp. 253-278.

Lower Nossob page: no phonology at all. Tuu languages page: only the family-level sentence that 'all languages in these three families also have tone'; nothing specific to Lower Nossob and no stress statement.

sources.citation: Starostin, George. 2015. Annotated Swadesh wordlists for the !Wi group (Peripheral Khoisan family): ǀXam, ǁNg!ke, ǂKhomani, Nǀuu, ǁXegwi, ǀʼAuni [kwi-aun], ǀHaasi [kwi-haa]. Global Lexicostatistical Database, text version 16/08/2015, 74 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone for ǀʼAuni/ǀHaasi; its transcription notes concern clicks only (pp. 5-8, e.g. Bleek 1937 sometimes writes an explicit glottal stop after a click). Source notes (pp. 3-5): all ǀʼAuni data are Bleek's (1911 in Bleek 1929; 1936 in Bleek 1937/1956); all ǀHaasi data are Story's, published as 'Story 1999 = Robert Story, Kʼuǀhaːsi Manuscript, ed. Anthony Traill, Khoisan Forum Working Paper 13... accompanied with extensive notes by A. Traill, including noteworthy considerations on how to interpret Story's phonetic notation.' GLD cites 'Story 1999: 21' for ǀHaasi forms.

sources.citation: Bleek, Dorothea F. 1956. A Bushman Dictionary (American Oriental Series 41). New Haven: American Oriental Society. ǀauni = SIV (D.B.), khatia = SIVa, kiǀhazi = SIVb (St. = R. Story, MS Collections of the Kiǀhazi dialect of Bushman, 1937).
sources.note: No statement. The editor's introduction reviews Bleek's transcription (IPA plus Doke's symbols, click symbols, pressed vowels, dropped diacritics) but never mentions tone or stress marking; the front matter contains no 'tone', 'stress' or 'accent' remark. Per-letter notes mention tone only for other languages (e.g. NII entries 'tone not ascertained'). It does confirm that Story's Kiǀhazi manuscript (1937) exists and is used as SIVb.

sources.citation: Bleek, Dorothea F. 1937. ǀAuni vocabulary. Bantu Studies 11(1): 259-278. DOI 10.1080/02561751.1937.9676055.
sources.note: Nothing. Alphabetical wordlist with no preface; some entries carry acute accents, macrons and a raised/lowered dash before the word (e.g. abú, áke, _ba, ¯ai) that are nowhere explained in the article (they match the marks Bleek used elsewhere, but the article itself gives no key).
Nothing; lists only the three descriptive refs (Bleek 1937 x2, Traill 1999) plus Güldemann 2014 for subclassification.
